rows.notes: The cited paper is a narrative review of remote sensing (hyperspectral, visible light/canopy colour, UAV, satellite) for plant nutrition diagnosis. It reports no data, experiment, survey or model runs of its own; all tables and results (e.g. Table 1 rice N and NDVI, Table 2 rape N regressions, Table 3 UAV winter wheat LNC models) are reproduced from other authors' work. The forward-looking statement about satellite, UAV and IoT increasingly enhancing real-time nutrition diagnosis is an opinion/outlook in the abstract and conclusions, not a finding. The conclusions actually caution that remote sensing alone is not accurate enough for nutrition diagnosis and fertilization recommendation and must be combined with traditional soil and plant testing.
